statement: One canonical verification policy derives fail-closed affected, pre-push, and release proof plans; all hooks, Solver consumers, CI, and publishers execute those plans or validate PASS-only content-addressed receipts, no legacy selector remains authoritative, and repeated verification of unchanged inputs is skipped without weakening any proof obligation.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

scripts/checks/change-selection.js is the sole semantic test-selection authority. Reverse-import evidence is additive only, legacy proof-cone consumers are migrated atomically, and no third selector or second impact matcher may remain.

Unreadable Git state, invalid taxonomy or impact contracts, corrupt policy inputs, and parse failures produce a typed refusal and no receipt. A boundary reason or broad-suite request may never launder an authority failure into a passing result.

Only complete PASS receipts may suppress a rerun. Their canonical semantic-input digest binds change semantics, file modes, symlinks, deletions, untracked bytes, policy and runner closure, registries and manifests, lockfile, toolchain, platform, and test-affecting environment while inert Solver bookkeeping is excluded.

Affected verification binds the final staged index or explicit range; pre-push covers every non-delete pushed ref with the deduplicated union of its affected plan and test:fast plus retained push obligations; release uses one proof DAG whose leaf identities execute at most once per valid receipt.
Version 1 gates known broad command identities and records measured timings. It does not refuse tests from an uncalibrated predicted-duration model and does not claim temporal exactly-once execution.

The cutover preserves existing static, model, focused-contract, owner-debt, golden-capability, bootstrap, integration, and release obligations; consolidation may deduplicate identical leaves but may not remove a proof requirement.
